deep.reconstruction:
The page has three layers. Context: this is the genus-3 (plane quartic, 28 bitangents, theta characteristics) material of R.AbelTheta. The previous page works with 3x2 characteristic matrices and Riemann's normal form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 with parameters alpha, beta, gamma.

(A) Pair-symbol calculus (top half). The symbol 'ij' (i,j in 1..7) denotes a quantity indexed by an unordered pair. On this page it behaves symmetrically (52 is used for 25). The context suggests bitangent or characteristic labels, or possibly squared distances, since the next page has Cayley-Menger/Gram determinants in r_ij^2. The meaning is not fixed by the page itself.
- Riemann expands products of 'Gram-like' trinomials, e.g. (12+13-23)(-46-36+34) + (-14-15+45)(26+56-52) + ... If ij were a squared distance r_ij^2, 12+13-23 would equal 2<v2-v1,v3-v1>.
- He collects the results into a 12-term cyclic sum: 46(23-13)+12(34-36)+14(25-56)+26(45-15)+56(12-23)+36(14-45)+15(46-34)+45(13-12)+23(15-14)+25(36-46)+34(56-26)+13(26-25).
- He regroups it as six two-term blocks (left column), e.g. 23(15-14)+45(13-12), 13(26-25)+56(12-23), 12(34-36)+46(23-13), ...
- He also writes the 'quadratic' forms (23-13)(36-34)-12*46, (45-15)(56-25)-14*26, (13-12)(15-14)+23*45, (36-46)(56-26)+34*25. These are the same shape as the systematic table on the next page.
- A right column repeats the six blocks after an index substitution introducing the index 7.
- A third attempt groups four-term brackets: 23(15-14+46-56), 21(34-36+56-45), 25(36-46+14-13), 26( ... [unfinished].
- A line of reciprocal products (1/64)(1/34)+(1/62)(1/51)+... is unrelated in form. It probably connects to the next page's partial-fraction work with m_6.

(B) Combinatorial tables. The triples 123, 145, 256, 346 have pairwise intersections 1,2,3,5,4,6. They form the four lines and six vertices of a complete quadrilateral. Riemann lists next to them the three pairs of opposite vertices (vertex pairs not on a common line): 16, 24, 35 (written 53). In the second table, 123, 145, 247, 357 is again a complete quadrilateral, on vertices 1,2,3,4,5,7, and he correctly lists the opposite pairs 17, 34, 25. These pairings presumably organize the blocks in (A). The next page repeats the same tables.

(C) Algebraic computation (bottom). One quantity t is represented in three ways:
t = a0^2 P0 + r0^2 = a1^2 P1 + r1^2 = a2^2 P2 + r2^2, with P0=pq, P1=p'q', P2=p''q''.
- Hence a_i^2 P_i - a_j^2 P_j = r_j^2 - r_i^2, written correctly on the page for all three pairs.
- Define f^2 = P0 P1 t, phi^2 = P0 P2 t, psi^2 = P1 P2 t. The phi entry is written with a stray alpha^2 on the page.
- [mine] Then a1^2 f^2 - a2^2 phi^2 = P0 t (a1^2 P1 - a2^2 P2) = P0 t (r2^2 - r1^2), and cyclically:
  - a2^2 psi^2 - a0^2 f^2 = P1 t (r0^2 - r2^2);
  - a0^2 phi^2 - a1^2 psi^2 = P2 t (r1^2 - r0^2).
- Each is a difference of squares on both sides. Riemann splits each factorization with a proportionality constant lambda:
  - a1 f + a2 phi = (a0/lambda) P0 (r1+r2) and a1 f - a2 phi = (lambda/a0) t (r1 - r2) [page sign];
  - analogously a2 psi ± a0 f, with constant mu/lambda and factors (r2 ± r0) P1;
  - and a0 phi ± a1 psi, with factors (r0 ± r1) P2.
- Adding the first pair gives the line written mid-left: a1 sqrt(P0 P1 t) = (a0/lambda) P0 (r1+r2) + (lambda/a0) t (r1 - r2), up to a factor 2.
- The aim is to express the square-root functions f, phi, psi linearly via r's and conic/linear factors. This yields linear relations among square roots of products, analogous to Riemann's relation sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 for the bitangents. Plausibly t is a quartic and p, q, r are conics, as in the representations F = Q1Q2 - Q3^2 of a plane quartic, but this is not explicit on the page.
errors: Sign convention in (C): from t = a^2 pq + r^2, one gets a1^2 f^2 - a2^2 phi^2 = pq(r''^2 - r'^2)t. The page writes pq(r'^2 - r''^2)t, and the analogous p'q' and p''q'' lines are also sign-flipped. All signs would be consistent with t = r^2 - a^2 pq instead, so either the convention changed or a systematic sign slip occurred.

The transcribed 'alpha'^2 phi^2 - alpha''^2 f^2' pairs the coefficients wrongly: only alpha'^2 f^2 - alpha''^2 phi^2 reduces (with f^2 = pq p'q' t, phi^2 = pq p''q'' t). The later factorizations alpha' f ± alpha'' phi show the intended pairing.
In alpha phi + alpha' psi = (alpha''/lambda)(r''+r') p''q'', the factor should be (r + r'), since the difference-of-squares factor is r^2 - r'^2.
The stray alpha^2 in 'phi = pq p''q'' alpha^2 t' is inconsistent with f^2 and psi^2. phi is also written without the square.
Factor 2 dropped when adding alpha' f + alpha'' phi and alpha' f - alpha'' phi to get the formula for alpha' sqrt(pq p'q' t).
Right-column table entry 24(37-37) is identically zero, an evident slip (presumably 24(37-34) or similar).
The splitting with a single constant lambda is an ansatz. Its consistency across the three pairs (lambda, mu) is not checked on the page.

results.what: Complete-quadrilateral incidence tables: lines 123,145,256,346 with opposite vertex pairs 16,24,35; lines 123,145,247,357 with opposite pairs 17,34,25
results.modern_name: complete quadrilateral / diagonal pairs (substructure of Fano-plane and Steiner-complex combinatorics of the 28 bitangents)
results.usually_credited_to: classical (Steiner, Hesse, Cayley 1850s for the bitangent combinatorics)

results.what: Expansion of products of trinomials in pair symbols into a 12-term cyclic sum, regrouped into six blocks of type (ab-ac)(ad-ae) ± bc*de
results.modern_name: bookkeeping for quadratic relations among pair-indexed quantities (bitangent or theta-characteristic relations)

results.what: Three representations t = a^2 pq + r^2 used to derive differences of squares and to split them linearly, giving linear relations among sqrt(pq p'q' t), sqrt(pq p''q'' t), sqrt(p'q' p''q'' t)
results.modern_name: square-root relations from representations of a quartic as Q1Q2 - Q3^2 (Steiner complexes); method behind the Riemann/Aronhold bitangent relations
results.usually_credited_to: Hesse, Steiner, Aronhold (1850s-1864); Riemann's p=3 paper (posthumous, Weber 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: These are scratch calculations within Riemann's known genus-3 theta/bitangent program, which Weber published posthumously in 1876. The algebra is elementary and the combinatorics classical. Nothing goes beyond what is known to be his.

checkable.asserts: Given t = a1^2 P1 + r1^2 = a2^2 P2 + r2^2, with f^2=P0 P1 t and phi^2=P0 P2 t: a1^2 f^2 - a2^2 phi^2 = P0 t (r2^2 - r1^2), the opposite sign to the page.
Second cyclic difference: a''^2 psi^2 - a^2 f^2 = p'q' t (r^2 - r''^2).
Third cyclic difference: a^2 phi^2 - a'^2 psi^2 = p''q'' t (r'^2 - r^2), so the linear factors involve (r ± r'), not (r'' + r').

checkable.sympy: a,l,P0,r1,r2,t=symbols('a l P0 r1 r2 t'); simplify((a/l*P0*(r1+r2))*(l/a*t*(r2-r1)) - P0*t*(r2**2-r1**2))==0
checkable.asserts: The lambda-splitting of the difference of squares is consistent (with the corrected sign).

checkable.sympy: from itertools import combinations; L=[{1,2,3},{1,4,5},{2,5,6},{3,4,6}]; sorted([tuple(A&B) for A,B in combinations(L,2)])==[(1,),(2,),(3,),(4,),(5,),(6,)]
checkable.asserts: 123,145,256,346 form a complete quadrilateral: each pair of triples meets in exactly one point, all six points distinct.

checkable.sympy: L=[{1,2,3},{1,4,5},{2,4,7},{3,5,7}]; pts=[1,2,3,4,5,7]; opp=sorted(tuple(sorted((i,j))) for i in pts for j in pts if i<j and not any(i in X and j in X for X in L)); opp==[(1,7),(2,5),(3,4)]
checkable.asserts: Opposite-vertex pairs of the quadrilateral 123,145,247,357 are 17,25,34, as listed on the page.

checkable.sympy: L=[{1,2,3},{1,4,5},{2,5,6},{3,4,6}]; pts=range(1,7); sorted((i,j) for i in pts for j in pts if i<j and not any(i in X and j in X for X in L))==[(1,6),(2,4),(3,5)]
checkable.asserts: Opposite pairs of the first quadrilateral are 16,24,35, as listed (written 16,24,53).

transcription_corrections: '625' and '643' in the triple table are the triples 256 and 346, with complementary pairs 16, 24, 53(=35).

The relations among squares are written with alpha'/alpha'' pairings matching the later factorizations alpha'f ± alpha''phi, i.e. alpha'^2 f^2 - alpha''^2 phi^2. The transcribed 'alpha'^2 phi^2 - alpha''^2 f^2' is likely a misreading or slip.
The mid-left formula reads alpha' sqrt(pq p'q' t) = (alpha/lambda) pq (r'+r'') + (lambda/alpha) t (r'-r''); the leading crossed symbol is a deleted alpha.
't t = pq + sqrt(p'q'p''q'')' is a garbled reading; the image shows an aborted line involving sqrt(p'q'p''q'').
Right-column entry '24(37-37)' is as written but is a slip.
The line 'f^2 x y z t u v w p = f^2 / x y z t alpha'v'w'p' = phi^2' is uncertain; it appears to define f^2 and phi^2 as products of factors.
